cases.name: Athena Castillo
cases.about: In an impromptu statement before sentencing, Amy Castillo reminded the court of all she had lost when her ex-husband took the lives of their children. Anthony, 6, was a mama's boy who never got to finish kindergarten, very smart and very loving, she said. Austin, 4, was a "wild kid, like his father" with a great sense of humor. Athena, 2, had just begun to talk. "I never even got to hear what she had to say," Amy Castillo said.
cases.narrative: He picked his 3 children up for a scheduled visit, and spent the day at the Maryland Science Center before checking into the Camden Yards Marriott. They ate dinner - room service - then Mark set the boys up with a computer game and took Athena into the bathroom to draw a bath. He held her tiny frame under the water for a full 10 minutes, timed with a stopwatch, until he was sure she was dead.
cases.disclaimer: CONVICTION

She co-owned operated a local bartending business called Mr. Mixology. Her Go Fund Me said, "Amy was an amazing daughter, sister, granddaughter, niece, aunt, cousin, and friend. If you knew her or even crossed her path once, you know how bright her light shined."

Her obituary said, "If you know Pooks you know she loves dirty martinis, salami, her cats - Willie & Charlie, but most of all her family. Her favorite place in the world is watching the sunset in Grandi's backyard. You wouldn't be surprised to catch her blaring 'Beautiful Crazy' by Luke Combs in her white Jeep. She is the life of any party & also the chillest Armstrong in the family.
Her presence is the calm hug you didn't know you needed. She will forever be a bright light in everyone's heart."
